title: Understanding N-grams
text: Think about how N-grams work. They capture sequences of letters, but do they consider the biological significance of codons?

title: Non-consecutive Segments
text: Consider how N-grams might treat sequences that aren't directly next to each other. How does this affect the representation of DNA sequences?

title: Meaningless Segments
text: What happens when N-grams capture sequences shorter than a codon? Do these shorter sequences have any biological meaning?

title: Overlapping Segments
text: Think about how overlapping segments might be formed in N-grams. How does this affect the interpretation of DNA sequences?

title: Wrap-around Segments
text: Consider how N-grams might treat the end of a sequence. Does it assume continuity where there is none?

hintAnswer: Segments with $$1$$ or $$2$$ letters have no meaning, which $$N-gram$$ would capture as "words".
title: Evaluating N-gram Segments
text: Which of the following is a reason why N-grams might capture segments that don't make sense biologically?
choices: Segments of $$non-consecutive$$ letters would be included, meaning ATGCA could suggest the word AGA.
Segments with $$1$$ or $$2$$ letters have no meaning, which $$N-gram$$ would capture as "words".
Overlapping segments would be included, meaning ATGCA is broken up into $$3$$ overlapping words.
DNA does not "wrap around", but $$N-gram$$ would capture $$"wrap-around"$$ segments, like TGG from GGTT.
